target: Vem har nyckeln under veckan alltid?
english: Who has the key during the week always?
tip: When the question word IS the subject, no inversion: Vem + verb.

target: Han frågade om jag hade lust att följa med ut.
english: He asked if I felt like coming along.
tip: Reported questions use "om" (if/whether) for yes/no questions.

target: Oj, det var dyrt, jag hade inte väntat mig det.
english: Oh, that was expensive, I had not expected that.
tip: vänta sig means to expect, not just wait: hade inte väntat mig det = hadn't expected it.

english: The train rolls into the station.
tip: Particle verbs put the stress on the particle: rullar in (rolls in), where in adds the direction into.

english: Midsummer is celebrated in June.
tip: Use i before a month name to mean in that month: i juni means in June.

english: The filmjölk is served with crispbread.
tip: Add -s to a verb for the passive: serverar (serves) becomes serveras (is served), no doer needed.

english: It is a quarter past nine.
tip: kvart means a quarter hour in clock talk: kvart över nio is a quarter past nine.

target: Kan du rekommendera en bra bok att läsa i sommar?
english: Can you recommend a good book to read this summer?
tip: 'Kan' (can) – doesn't change form. The main verb stays infinitive: 'Jag kan simma' (I can swim).

target: Vad synd att du inte kunde komma med oss idag!
english: What a shame that you could not come with us today!
tip: After att, inte sits before the verb: att du inte kunde komma. English never moves 'not' like this.

target: Hon läste hela boken på bara tre dagar under semestern.
english: She read the whole book in just three days during vacation.
tip: på plus a time span tells how long something took: på tre dagar = in three days.

target: Vi tackade honom för den goda middagen och det fina sällskapet.
english: We thanked him for the good dinner and the nice company.
tip: Double definiteness shows in both genders: den goda middagen (en) and det fina sällskapet (ett).

english: He is a teacher.
tip: Swedish drops the article for jobs after är: Han är lärare, not han är en lärare.

english: The sandwich is good.
tip: For food that tastes good use god, not bra: Smörgåsen är god means the sandwich is tasty.

english: I need a vacation.
tip: Semester means vacation, not a school term: Jag behöver semester = I need time off.

english: We fell asleep late.
tip: somna = fall asleep (the moment); sova = to sleep (the state): vi somnade sent.

english: Sunday is a day of rest.
tip: Days of the week stay lowercase in Swedish, so söndag is written small in mid-sentence.

english: I can't afford it.
tip: Ha råd is the set phrase for affording something: har inte råd = can't afford it.

english: I have no idea.
tip: Before an en-word, no is ingen: ingen aning. Ett-words take inget, plurals take inga.

english: Better late than never.
tip: Än means than after a comparative like bättre: bättre sent än aldrig = better late than never.

english: We each have our own fika.
tip: Varsin means one each: Vi tar varsin fika = we each get our own fika.

english: That's a good question.
tip: Bra never changes form for gender, number, or definiteness: en bra fråga, det är bra.

english: I noticed the change.
tip: Lägga märke till is the fixed phrase for to notice: lade märke till = noticed.

english: In short it works well.
tip: When Kort sagt opens the sentence, the verb fungerar comes before the subject det.

english: I am allergic to nuts.
tip: Allergic to is allergisk mot, using mot rather than till or för: allergisk mot nötter.

english: The beautiful flowers smell nice.
tip: Gott takes the neuter -t here because it describes the verb doftar, not a noun. Adverbs use the -t form: doftar gott.

english: We checked in at the hotel.
tip: checka in = check in; in is a separable particle after the verb: vi checkade in.

target: Vi ses där varje dag nog!
english: See you there every day probably!
tip: The -s on ses makes it reciprocal: vi ses = we see each other, the usual way to say see you.

target: Vi såg en fin film igår.
english: We saw a nice movie yesterday.
tip: se is irregular in the past: se becomes såg = saw: vi såg en film.

target: Jag kommer så fort jag kan.
english: I'll come as soon as I can.
tip: Så fort literally means so fast but works as as soon as: så fort jag kan = as soon as I can.

target: Vi tyckte om maten på stationen.
english: We liked the food at the station.
tip: tycka om means to like; om is a stressed particle: vi tyckte om maten.
